| Category = Recipes for flatbread
| Yield = 8 pitas
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}
__NOTOC__

'''Pita''' (also known as ''pita bread'', ''Arabic bread'' etc.) is a [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeasted]] [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] flatbread originating from North-African, to Middle-Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines. It is usually eaten with sauces, dips and fillings. Dishes that use pita include [[Cookbook:Kebab|kebab]], [[Cookbook:Gyros|gyros]], and [[Cookbook:Shwarma|shwarma]]. 

==Ingredients==
* 250 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) warm water
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] instant [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]]
* 500 ml (2 cups or 17 fl oz) durum [[Cookbook:Wheat|wheat]] flour

== Procedure ==
# Dissolve the yeast in a bowl of warm water. Add salt, oil and flour, mix it, and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] it into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]].
# Let the dough rise to twice its size.
# Divide the risen dough into 8 pieces and shape them into balls.
# Then roll the balls into flat and round pita breads (to a diameter of 15 cm or 6 inches).
# Let the breads rise in a warm place covered with a cloth for about 30 minutes.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 225°C (435°F) for about 12 minutes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Cut the bread into two pieces so it can be used like a sandwich filled with salad or meat. Or the exact same, wrapped into a roll.
* Pita is delicious when dipped in sauces. There are lots of possible ideas and combinations!
* Because this is a sticky dough, avoid using extra flour to dust your dough when working with it. Grease your hands and work surface with an oil of your choice.
